entry: 2026-09-09 — Fake GitHub API vs GitHub API switch

verification.summary: The check is falsifiable for the issue-line and loading-phase assertions, but the spec's own description of the indicator as "self-updating" contradicts the check's requirement that each dot-phase appear as a distinct, complete stdout line, leaving the implementer to guess which reading to satisfy. Traceability is unchecked — I was not given the conversation this spec was agreed in.

mustFix.quote: appends each newly-seen open issue as a line above a self-updating loading indicator
mustFix.problem: "Self-updating" naturally reads as in-place overwrite (e.g. carriage-return redraw), which would never emit 'Loading .', 'Loading ..', 'Loading ...' as three separate newline-terminated lines. An implementer following this description would fail `grep -qxF` in test.bash, which requires each phase as its own exact line; the spec does not say which reading governs.

shouldFix.quote: Use Exponential Backoff strategy to handle exceptions. Double the interval after each consecutive error, reset the counter on success.
shouldFix.problem: This is carried into the spec as a decided requirement (implicitly, via the 'Not this' row excluding only rate-limit handling 'beyond' backoff) but no Behaviour row or line in test.bash exercises an error/backoff path; the check can pass with backoff entirely unimplemented.

shouldFix.quote: Loading indicator always appears at the bottom, separated by whitespace line from the rest of the output.
shouldFix.problem: This decided formatting rule (blank-line separation between issue log and indicator) is not asserted anywhere in test.bash, so the check passes whether or not the separator is present.

shouldKnow.problem: Spec is marked unverified/draft with no PLAN.md step number filled in ('work-order step N'), so its place in the sequence and whether it has been run against real code cannot be confirmed from the file alone.
